cross_references.short_title: Cal. Vehicle Code §11711 — Dealer Fraud Treble Damages
cross_references.description: §11711 is the primary California civil remedy for the Jaguar XE yo-yo financing and dealer fraud facts. §11711 provides treble damages (up to 3× actual damages) + mandatory attorneys' fees for fraudulent acts or misrepresentations by licensed dealers. TILA establishes the federal standard for the financing disclosure violations; §11711 provides the California treble damages remedy for the same fraudulent misrepresentations.

cross_references.short_title: Cal. Civil Code §1750 — CLRA Consumer Legal Remedies Act
cross_references.description: CLRA prohibits misrepresenting the terms of a transaction (§1770(a)(14)) and making false statements of fact (§1770(a)(5)). Yo-yo financing where original disclosed terms are false = CLRA violation. CLRA provides actual damages, $1,000 minimum, punitive damages, injunction, and attorneys' fees. TILA and CLRA run simultaneously on the same auto financing facts.

cross_references.short_title: Bus. & Prof. Code §17200 — UCL Unfair Business Practices
cross_references.description: TILA violation = unlawful prong predicate for UCL §17200 claim. UCL adds 4-year SOL (longer than TILA's 1-year SOL), injunctive relief, and restitution. The yo-yo financing scheme independently qualifies as 'unfair' under the UCL balancing test. UCL SOL (4 years) may make the Jaguar XE TILA-predicate UCL claim viable where the direct TILA claim is time-barred.

cross_references.short_title: Cal. Civil Code §§2981-2984 — Rees-Levering Motor Vehicle Sales and Finance Act
cross_references.description: Rees-Levering is California's state auto financing disclosure law — the state parallel to federal TILA. For auto sales where the financing terms were misrepresented (yo-yo financing), Rees-Levering provides an independent state-law claim with a 4-year SOL that may not be time-barred for the 2018 Jaguar XE. Rees-Levering's remedies (voiding the contract, recovering payments made) may be more powerful than TILA's statutory damages for certain facts.
